content:
Each \(T\)-tetromino covers \(4\) unit squares.

### 1. Upper bound
The \(6\times6\) grid has \(36\) squares, so area alone gives
\[
N\le \left\lfloor\frac{36}{4}\right\rfloor=9.
\]

Now color the grid like a chessboard. It has \(18\) squares of each color. Every \(T\)-tetromino covers either:

- \(3\) black and \(1\) white square, or
- \(1\) black and \(3\) white squares.

If \(9\) tetrominoes filled the grid, the number of black squares they covered would be the sum of \(9\) odd numbers, hence odd. But the grid has \(18\) black squares, an even number. Therefore \(9\) tetrominoes are impossible, so
\[
N\le 8.
\]

### 2. Construction with eight pieces
The following placement uses eight \(T\)-tetrominoes; equal letters form one piece, and dots are uncovered squares:

\[
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
A&A&A&B&E&\cdot\\ \hline
C&A&B&B&E&E\\ \hline
C&C&D&B&E&\cdot\\ \hline
C&D&D&D&\cdot&F\\ \hline
G&G&G&H&F&F\\ \hline
\cdot&G&H&H&H&F\\ \hline
\end{array}
\]

Each letter indeed forms a rotated \(T\), and no two pieces overlap. Hence the upper bound is attainable.

\[
\boxed{8}
\]
